simple: A plastic rod kept burning at 13.6% oxygen in space but stopped at 16% on Earth.
expert: In BASS-II microgravity concurrent stagnation-point flow, a ¼-inch PMMA rod sustained steady flame spread at 13.6% oxygen; 1-g blowoff occurred at 16% oxygen.

simple: For thin plastic sheets, flames died out below about 2 cm/s of airflow and blew out near 40 cm/s.
expert: For 0.1 mm thick PMMA sheets in opposed flow, flames radiatively quenched below 2 cm/s and neared blow-off extinction at 40 cm/s.

simple: The station's smoke detector missed Kapton smoke in half the SAME tests.
expert: During microgravity SAME tests, the ISS smoke detector failed to alarm for Kapton smoke in half of the tests.

simple: Large fuel drops kept burning with an invisible cool flame after the visible flame went out.
expert: In microgravity at 0.5-1.0 atm and 14%-25% oxygen by volume, large n-heptane, n-octane, and n-decane droplets burned quasi-steadily as low-temperature cool flames after visible-flame radiative extinction.

simple: No solid material in PSI was tested above about 22% oxygen, but a Moon base may use 30% or more.
expert: BASS-II tests peaked at 22.2% oxygen and had no tests at 30% or more; Moon base air may use 30% oxygen or more.
